aAbout: Ventusky visualises forecast-model data — wind, precipitation, temperature, pressure, clouds, snow and waves — as exceptionally clean animated maps, including wind flows at different altitudes. It draws on the ECMWF, GFS, ICON and GEM models (per its premium page) and adds radar, satellite and air-quality layers. Access is free with an optional premium tier; it is weather-only, deliberately, with no webcams, tracking or extras competing for attention.
aStrengths: Ventusky is the cleaner forecast reader: uncluttered, legible maps built from four global models — ECMWF, GFS, ICON and GEM — where wind and precipitation patterns over the coming days are easy to follow, with wind flows at different altitudes that aviation-minded users appreciate and an air-quality layer on top. If your job is to read the weather that is coming, especially wind and rain, Ventusky's meteorological focus and restraint beat a live-satellite view.
bAbout: Zoom Earth, by Neave Interactive Limited, is an interactive weather map of the world and a real-time hurricane tracker, free on the web, iOS and Android. It shows near real-time satellite imagery — live images from NOAA GOES, JMA Himawari and EUMETSAT Meteosat geostationary satellites updated every 10 minutes, plus HD images updated twice a day from NASA polar-orbiting satellites Aqua and Terra — alongside rain radar with nowcasting, forecast maps from DWD ICON and NOAA GFS, hurricane tracking using NHC, JTWC, NRL and IBTrACS data, and an active fires overlay from NASA FIRMS. No account is required for basic use; an account is optional and lets you access a subscription across devices.
bStrengths: Zoom Earth is the better live watch: satellite imagery refreshed every 10 minutes from three geostationary fleets, HD passes twice a day from NASA Aqua and Terra, rain radar with nowcasting for the next minutes, a hurricane tracker fed by NHC, JTWC, NRL and IBTrACS, and NASA FIRMS fire detections — all free, on web and mobile, with no account needed to start. If a storm is happening now, Zoom Earth shows it as it unfolds rather than as a model predicted it.
betterAnswer: For forecast depth, Ventusky is better: four global models, altitude wind and the cleanest presentation of the days ahead. For live conditions, Zoom Earth is better: 10-minute satellite imagery, radar nowcasting and best-in-class hurricane tracking, all free with no account. Start with the question you ask most — 'what is coming?' points to Ventusky, 'what is happening now?' points to Zoom Earth.

intro: Ventusky and Zoom Earth are both free weather maps you open when something is happening outside — and they start from opposite ends of the same data. Ventusky is the forecast-model tool: clean animated maps of wind, rain and temperature drawn from ECMWF, GFS, ICON and GEM, including wind flows at different altitudes. Zoom Earth is the live-observation tool: satellite imagery updated every 10 minutes, rain radar with nowcasting and a dedicated hurricane tracker, with forecast layers from ICON and GFS underneath. Which one suits you depends on whether you read the forecast or watch the sky as it is now.
pricingA: Free access with an optional premium option, billed via the web or the app stores. Ventusky does not publish a single public price list and prices vary by region and store, so we won't quote a figure we can't verify — check the premium page in your region.
pricingB: Free on the web, iOS and Android, with no account required for basic use. Zoom Earth Pro is listed under In-App Purchases on the official US App Store listing at $1.99 and $11.99 — that listing does not label which billing period each price corresponds to, so the period for each price is unverified. Its terms say subscriptions are billed on a periodic basis (e.g. monthly or annually), as specified at the time of purchase. No free trial for Pro was stated on the official pages checked.

verdictA: Choose Ventusky if you plan by the forecast — sailing, flying, hiking or trip planning over the next days — and want the clearest possible picture of wind, rain and temperature, including wind aloft, with the least interface between you and the models.
verdictB: Choose Zoom Earth if you watch weather as it happens — a hurricane approaching, a storm line crossing, smoke from a wildfire — and want live satellite, radar nowcasting and storm tracking in a simple free app.
verdictLine: Ventusky looks forward: the deepest, cleanest read on what the models say is coming. Zoom Earth looks at now: live satellite and radar, refreshed every 10 minutes, built around storms in progress. Forecast readers start with Ventusky; storm-watchers start with Zoom Earth — most weather watchers end up keeping both.
worldEye: Neither Ventusky nor Zoom Earth shows you the ground itself — one shows model output, the other shows cloud tops. WorldEye adds the missing layer: a free 3D globe with 74,229 public cameras across 105 countries, so you can check the actual conditions in a place alongside live flights, ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes and wildfires, with a free tier and no signup. It is not a forecast-model platform and does not pretend to match either specialist on meteorological depth. Its optional Pro tier is $7.99/week · $13.99/month · $74.99/year.
